text: A linear chain of three masses: a learning bar at one end, a community commons at the other, and a civic hinge between them. The hinge gathers the school's public face (arrival, the office, the arts and the library) and acts as front door and crossroads, so every passage between learning and commons crosses it.

A linear chain of three masses: a learning bar at one end, a community commons at the other, and a civic hinge between them. The hinge gathers the school's public face (arrival, the office, the arts and the library) and acts as front door and crossroads, so every passage between learning and commons crosses it. Aims to give the school one legible front where visitors, families and daily student movement meet, while keeping classrooms quiet at the far end of the chain and the commons reachable for community use.

The classroom mass holds core academic on floors 1-3; special education on floors 1-2. The commons mass holds physical education (gym) on floor 1; dining and food service on floor 1. The third mass holds art and music on floors 1-2; media center on floor 3; medical on floor 1; administration and guidance on floor 1; custodial and maintenance on floor 1. Direct links join the classroom mass and the third mass; the commons mass and the third mass. There is no direct link between the classroom mass and the commons mass.

A compact closed cluster in which the shared realm is layered vertically: the commons volume forms the base and an arts loft rides on its roof, making one cultural block for gathering, performance and making. A civic block crowned by the library and a plain academic bar complete a triangle, each mass joined to both others.

A community pavilion for athletics and dining can open on its own. A low civic-arts pavilion sits at arrival with the library above the office. Movement between the pavilions is outdoors.
